title: Automate your sales pipeline
description: Let Strawberry find customers, prep your calls, log them without a bot, and follow up, so the pipeline keeps moving while you sell.
introduction: Most of sales isn't selling. It's everything around it: digging through LinkedIn, copying notes into the CRM, and writing the same follow-up for the fortieth time.

Strawberry is a browser with an AI teammate built in. It works in LinkedIn, your inbox, your CRM, and the open web the same way you do, and it remembers your customers between tasks. Start with one job. Over time it can run most of the cycle: finding leads, booking meetings, logging calls, following up, and even answering customers once they've signed.

blocks.text: Not sure where to start? Your companion can look at the work you have open and suggest the first thing worth handing over.

skill.context: Ask your companion to look at your work and suggest the first thing to hand over.

blocks.text: Tell Strawberry who your best customers are, or let it learn that from your website and CRM. It searches the places lead databases miss, like niche directories, job posts, and funding news, and brings back a short list with a reason and a source for every company. You correct a small sample first, so the big run goes to the right companies.

items.context: Get a first sample of prospects, each with a reason it fits and the source behind it.

blocks.text: Before a call, Strawberry pulls together who's in the room, what changed at their company, and what you talked about last time. Then it works out with you what your strongest ammunition is, so your notes are ready before you join.

sections.title: Log calls without a bot in the room

blocks.text: Strawberry's transcription records the call on your own computer, so nobody has to admit a note-taker. When you hang up, the follow-up email, the CRM notes, and the next steps are already drafted for you to check.

sections.title: Follow up without the spreadsheet gymnastics

blocks.text: Strawberry writes outreach from your own sent emails, so it sounds like you and not like a sequence tool. It can run a drip of follow-ups, track them in a sheet, and stop the moment someone replies. Nothing sends without your say-so.

sections.title: Find the buyers already using your product

blocks.text: Some of your best leads already have an account. A weekly Routine can look through your user database or product analytics for accounts behaving like buyers, and hand you each one with the reason it stood out.

items: Find companies from signals: a new funding round, a relevant job post, a new office, a switch away from a competitor.
Enrich a list you already have with decision-makers, emails, and company size.
Keep the pipeline healthy: stale leads, duplicates, and contacts who changed jobs.
Create a Slack channel for every new deal, with the right people already in it.
Pin a live pipeline dashboard as a tab.
Make a one-pager or a short deck for a specific account, in your brand.

blocks.text: Once something works for you, it can work for the whole team. Save the method as a team skill and every rep's companion sources, preps, and follows up the same way. Share the companion itself and it brings everything it has learned about your customers along.

Put the steady parts on a Routine and the pipeline gets worked every morning, whether or not anyone remembered to. At that point it stops feeling like a tool and starts feeling like a colleague who joined the sales team and never drops a thread.
